title: ECG–PPG respiratory-rate discrepancy improves an additive error-risk model across two public cohorts
abstract: Adding ECG–PPG respiratory-rate discrepancy to an additive summary model reduced Brier loss by 0.021042 in BIDMC (95% record-bootstrap CI 0.009719–0.032646) and 0.024792 in independent CapnoBase (0.007888–0.043129). A flexible-baseline challenge removed decisive internal benefit; these are exploratory measurement-reliability results, not clinical validation. We fitted equal-record ridge logistic models using 53 adult ICU recordings and transported frozen models to 42 independent perioperative adult/pediatric recordings. The target was PPG respiratory-rate error greater than5 breaths/min, not disease. Both individual estimated rates were already included in the comparator. Dataset reuse, detector limitations, conditional uncertainty and model-form dependence limit the finding.
